core_obligations: Part (b) implies (a): an equivalence of categories is in particular fully faithful (proof lines 1517).

Part (a) implies (c), by contraposition: if f is not universally injective, find a module M such that the base change map on M has nontrivial kernel N, and show that the projection from M to its quotient by N is not an isomorphism while its image under base extension is, so that base extension is not fully faithful (proof lines 1517-1522).

Part (c) implies (b): for a descent datum, use the two earlier lemmas to see that the natural map from the base extension of its pushforward back to it is an isomorphism of modules with descent data (proof lines 1525-1528).

For an arbitrary module M_0, use adjunction to identify the composite of the unit followed by the image of that isomorphism with the identity, conclude that the unit becomes an isomorphism after base extension, and then apply the outside criterion for universally injective ring maps to see that the unit itself is an isomorphism (proof lines 1529-1535).
Conclude that the pushforward and base extension functors are quasi-inverse, so that base extension is an equivalence of categories (proof lines 1536).
proof_roadmap: The trivial implication from effectiveness to full faithfulness (proof lines 1517).
From full faithfulness to universal injectivity, by exhibiting a quotient that base extension cannot distinguish (proof lines 1517-1522).
From universal injectivity to effectiveness: the counit is an isomorphism on descent data (proof lines 1525-1528).
The unit becomes an isomorphism after base extension, hence is one (proof lines 1529-1535).
Quasi-inverse functors and the conclusion (proof lines 1536).
difficulty_reason: For a ring map f the theorem asserts the equivalence of three conditions: that base extension along f on modules is fully faithful, that it is an equivalence of categories, and that f is universally injective (statement lines 1506-1514). Two of the three implications carry real work and they are of different kinds. The implication from full faithfulness to universal injectivity is proved by contraposition and requires a construction: if f is not universally injective then some module M has an element killed by the base change map, and the quotient by the submodule generated by such elements is not isomorphic to M although its image under base extension is an isomorphism, so base extension is not fully faithful (proof lines 1517-1522). The implication from universal injectivity to effectiveness is an adjunction argument: the counit of the adjunction between base extension and its right adjoint is an isomorphism on descent data by two earlier lemmas, and then the composite of the unit followed by the image of that counit is the identity by adjunction, which forces the unit on the image of base extension to be an isomorphism, whereupon a criterion for base change along a universally injective ring map upgrades this to the unit itself (proof lines 1525-1536). The claim is H3: the two directions rest on independent mechanisms, one a counterexample construction at the level of modules and one a formal adjunction computation whose final step needs an outside criterion.
